source_text: Quid est ergo renerti, quam in Christum credendo per eum qui est uia ueniendi ad patrem Deo reconciliatum posse saluari ? quomodo autem reuerti ad Deum possunt qui ei per quem est agnitio et reuersio ad Deum uoluntatem Dei praedicanti credere noluerunt ? aut quomodo Deum satisfactione placare poterunt, qui eum qui est satisfactio et placatio pro nobis apud patrem sacrilega impugnatione persequi maluerunt? si enim aduocatum Christum habemus apud Deum patrem, initiare utique ea quae nos docuit et monuit quaeque apud patrem locuturus est sollicito timore facere debemus. igitur nos qui mente in Domini metum prona mandatorum eius monitis insistimus et religiosi ac uenerabilis cordis fide credulitatem de eius timore concepimus, quid aliud sequi, quid cupere, quid magis uelle ac tenere debemus, quam ut omni a nobis mentis antiquae nocte discussa et caligine uitae prioris abstersa mandatorum Domini salutarium memores ac uitae aeternae promissa retinentes ad eius monita uertamur et in ipsius lumine quod ostendit firmata credulitate gradiamur: ut qui ignari aliquando salutis futurae in erroribus implicati uitae prioris ac tenebris oberrauimus inluminati nunc eius ueri luminis claritate et ostenso nobis atque patefacto melioris uiae limite Domini mandata sequenda et gerenda teneamus.
thought_title: Return to God through Christ alone
orientation: The author is addressing Vigilius directly, explaining what true return to God means and urging that believers must follow Christ's commands in reverent fear.
pass_a_gloss: What therefore is it to return, than by believing in Christ to be able to be saved through him who is the way of coming to the Father, having been reconciled to God? But how can they return to God who were unwilling to believe him who preaches the will of God, through whom is the knowledge and return to God? Or how will they be able to appease God with satisfaction, who preferred to persecute with sacrilegious attack him who is the satisfaction and appeasement for us before the Father? For if we have Christ as advocate before God the Father, we ought certainly to do with anxious fear the things which he taught and warned us and which he is going to speak before the Father. Therefore we who with a mind inclined to the fear of the Lord press upon the warnings of his commandments and have conceived faith of believing from a religious and venerable heart from his fear, what else ought we to follow, what to desire, what rather to wish and hold, than that, with all the night of the old mind shaken off from us and the darkness of the former life wiped away, mindful of the saving commandments of the Lord and holding fast the promises of eternal life, we should turn to his warnings and walk in his own light which he showed with faith made firm: so that we who once, ignorant of the future salvation, entangled in the errors of the former life and its darkness, wandered about, now enlightened by the brightness of his true light and with the path of the better way shown to us and laid open, should hold to the commandments of the Lord as things to be followed and carried out.

choices.why: The source spelling renerti is a variant of reuerti; rendered as 'to return' to match the glossary's sense of turning back to God.
The gerund in the ablative expresses means; 'by believing' preserves the instrumental force of the Latin.
Both nouns describe Christ's atoning role; kept as a pair to preserve the rhetorical doubling of the source.
The term is a legal metaphor for Christ's intercessory role before the Father; 'advocate' preserves the courtroom imagery.
The phrase pairs anxiety with reverent fear; 'anxious fear' keeps both the emotional and religious dimensions.
Per the glossary, credulitas is rendered as 'faith' (believing faith), not 'credulity'.

bible_refs.note: aduocatum Christum habemus apud Deum patrem

pass_b_english: What does it mean to return, then, but to be saved by believing in Christ, through him who is the way of coming to the Father, having been reconciled to God? And how can they return to God, when they have refused to believe the one who preaches God's will, through whom there is knowledge and return to God? Or how will they be able to appease God with satisfaction, when they preferred to persecute with sacrilegious assault the one who is our satisfaction and appeasement before the Father? For if we have Christ as our advocate before God the Father, we must certainly carry out with anxious fear the things he taught and urged, and the things he is going to speak before the Father. Therefore we, who with minds inclined to the fear of the Lord press on in his commandments' warnings and have conceived faith from his fear with the faith of a reverent and worshipful heart—what else should we follow, what else desire, what else prefer and hold to, than that we shake off every night of our old mind and wipe away the darkness of our former life, remember the Lord's saving commandments, hold fast to the promises of eternal life, turn to his warnings, and walk in the light he has shown with faith made firm? Then we who once were ignorant of the salvation to come, entangled in the errors and darkness of our former life, now enlightened by the brightness of his true light, with the path of a better way shown and opened to us, may hold to the Lord's commandments, following them and doing them.

problems.source_quote: si enim aduocatum Christum habemus apud Deum patrem, initiare utique ea quae nos docuit et monuit quaeque apud patrem locuturus est sollicito timore facere debemus.
problems.why: The source does not cite 1 John 2:1; the English inserts a scriptural reference not present.
problems.ruling: Source has no scripture reference; English inserts "(1 John 2:1)" absent from Latin, misleading readers about the source text.

edits.old: before God the Father (1 John 2:1), we must
edits.new: before God the Father, we must

fixed: Removed the inserted scriptural citation '(1 John 2:1)'; the source has no such reference.

problems.quote: And how can they return to God who refused to believe the one through whom comes knowledge of God and return to God, when he preached God's will?
problems.source_quote: quomodo autem reuerti ad Deum possunt qui ei per quem est agnitio et reuersio ad Deum voluntatem Dei praedicanti credere noluerunt?
problems.why: English misattributes the refusal to God instead of the Jews and adds an extra clause, changing the meaning.
problems.fix: And how can they return to God, when they have refused to believe the one who preaches God's will, through whom there is knowledge and return to God?
problems.ruling: Source: 'credere noluerunt' = they refused to believe; 'praedicanti' agrees with 'ei per quem...' = the one preaching. English 'when he preached' misattributes refusal to God.

edits.old: And how can they return to God who refused to believe the one through whom comes knowledge of God and return to God, when he preached God's will?
edits.new: And how can they return to God, when they have refused to believe the one who preaches God's will, through whom there is knowledge and return to God?

fixed: The English misattributes the refusal to God instead of the Jews and adds an extra clause; the source reads 'qui ei per quem est agnitio et reuersio ad Deum voluntatem Dei praedicanti credere noluerunt' (they refused to believe the one who preaches God's will, through whom is knowledge and return to God).
